AcronymsTable.description: Acronyms that must be defined before they're used.

definitions.description: Regexes for where an acronym is defined, matched with case. The first group of each is the acronym it defines. By default, a word in parentheses after a word: "Portable Document Format (PDF)".

except.description: Acronyms that need no definition, such as "HTML" or "NASA".

match.description: A regex for an acronym where it's used, matched with case. Its first group, if it has one, is the acronym, so `APIs` can be a use of `API`. By default, three capital letters or more, with a plural `s`.

CapitalizationTable.description: How a block's words are capitalized.

except.description: Words and phrases to leave as written, such as names: "Proserunner", "Visual Studio Code".

style.description: The case to use: by default, "sentence".

oneOf.description: Any case matches, with Unicode case folding.
Only the case as written matches.

Entry.description: A word or pattern, or a table with `match` and its own `suggest`, `message`, `case` or `level`.

EntryTable.description: An entry with settings of its own.

case.description: Whether this entry ignores case, in place of the rule's `case`.

level.description: How serious this entry's issues are, in place of the rule's `level`. The rule's level in config replaces both.

message.description: The message for this entry's issues, in place of the rule's.

suggest.description: What to write instead, best first. Suggestions can use the same placeholders as messages, except `{suggestion}`.

Examples.description: Text that `proserunner rules test` checks a rule against.

bad.description: Text the rule must report an issue in.

fix.description: `[before, after]` pairs: replacing each issue in `before` with its first suggestion must give `after`.

good.description: Text the rule must report nothing in.

Except.description: A match never to report, or a table with a `pattern` that must match all of it.

ExceptTable.description: An exception written as a regex.

pattern.description: A regex that must match the whole match, with the rule's case.

Formula.description: A readability formula, which scores text as a school grade.

oneOf.description: Words per sentence and syllables per word.
Words per sentence, and the share of words with three syllables or more.
Letters and sentences per 100 words.
Characters per word and words per sentence.

LimitTable.description: How long a sentence or block may be.

per.description: What each count is of: by default, each "sentence".

oneOf.description: The whole document: every block the rule applies to. Its issue is at the first block's first sentence.
Each block.

MetricTable.description: A readability score to keep under a limit.

formula.description: The formula, each of which gives a U.S. school grade: by default, "flesch-kincaid".

min-words.description: Text with fewer words than this isn't scored: 100 by default.

per.description: What to score: by default, the whole "document".

Per.description: What a limit's count is of.

oneOf.description: Each sentence.
Each block: a paragraph, heading, list item or table cell.

Scope.description: Where in a document a rule applies. A rule with no scope applies to all prose.

oneOf.description: Paragraphs, footnotes and captions.
Headings and titles.
List items.
Table cells.
Quoted blocks, such as Markdown's `>` lines.
Code blocks, when checked (`--code-blocks`).
The first word capitalized, and the rest lowercase.
Every word capitalized but articles, conjunctions and short prepositions in the middle.

Term.description: A term as it must be written, or a table with `term` and other spellings to find in `match`.

TermTable.description: A term with other spellings or settings of its own.

level.description: How serious this term's issues are, in place of the rule's `level`.

match.description: Other spellings to find, in any case. Braces expand as in `words`.

message.description: The message for this term's issues, in place of the rule's.

term.description: The term, written the one right way.

oneOf.description: Words, with `it's`, `well-known` and `3.5` one word each.
Sentences, which don't end at abbreviations such as `e.g.` and `Dr.`.
Characters as the rules see them, spaces included. Hidden text, such as a URL or a quotation, is one, as "…" shows it.

description: A proserunner rule file. Its id is `<source>/<file name>`, such as `default/hedging` for the built-in `hedging.toml`.

acronyms.description: Report an acronym used before it's defined.

capitalization.description: Report words in a block, usually a heading, that the style capitalizes otherwise.

consistent.description: Groups of spellings a document keeps to one of, such as `[["advisor", "adviser"]]`: the first a document uses wins, and the others are reported. Braces expand as in `words`, the same way in each form of a group.

examples.description: Text that `proserunner rules test` checks the rule against.

except.description: Matches never to report, each compared with a whole match using the rule's case: a string, or `{ pattern = '…' }`, a regex that must match all of it.

explain.description: Why the rule exists, for `proserunner explain` and verbose output.

heading-levels.description: The headings the rule applies to, by level: 0 is a document's title, 1 its outermost sections, 2 the sections inside those. By default, every level. Other blocks are left to `scope`.

level.description: How serious the rule's issues are. A run fails on issues at the config's `fail-on` level or above.

limit.description: Report sentences or blocks longer than `max` words, sentences or characters.

message.description: The message for each issue. `{match}` stands for the match, `{suggestion}` for the entry's suggestions and `{rule}` for the rule's name. An entry's own `message` takes its place.

metric.description: Report text that reads above a school grade.

name.description: The name people see. By default it comes from the file name: `needless-variants.toml` is "Needless variants".

patterns.description: Regular expressions in Rust syntax, used exactly as written. Lookaround and backreferences work, with a limit on backtracking. Messages and suggestions can use their groups: `{1}`, `{name}`.

repeat.description: Report a word repeated right after itself, such as "the the".

scope.description: Where the rule applies. By default, everywhere.

terms.description: Names written exactly one way, such as "GitHub". Any case matches, and anything but the term as written is reported.

words.description: Words and phrases, matched literally. `{a,b}` expands, so `synerg{y,ies}` is two words. A space matches any run of whitespace, line breaks included. A word that starts or ends with a letter, digit or `_` must start or end a word in the text.
